summary:
The LIGHTSITE III 24-month analysis was published in *Retina* in 2026 by Jaffe et al. A total of 148 eyes (100 subjects) with dry AMD were randomized into the study. The trial was double-masked and sham-controlled, using multiwavelength PBM from the Valeda system at 590, 660, and 850 nm. The authors report that the trial met the prespecified primary BCVA efficacy end point at M21 with a significant difference between treatment groups (P = 0.0036) and a +6.2 letter gain after PBM. The follow-up ran 24 months, and extended three months beyond treatment completion to assess carryover effect.

Commentary has followed. A *Retina* editorial by Vavvas is titled "Promising Signal, Familiar Questions" (PubMed ID 42018574), and a separate piece by Zarbin addresses the 24-month results (PubMed ID 42024302). I did not retrieve the editorials' contents, so I can't say what they conclude.

A model-based cost-effectiveness analysis using the 24-month data found PBM to be cost-effective at conventional US willingness-to-pay thresholds, driven primarily by a 71.7% relative reduction in incident GA at 24 months. Its authors say coverage consideration should wait pending independent replication of the GA reduction and prospective EQ-5D data collection. That GA figure comes from a model, not a direct trial endpoint, so treat it with caution.
